question.leadin: In 1997, this country moved its capital from Almaty, its largest city.
question.text: Name this Central Asian country with capital at Nur-Sultan, renamed from Astana in 2019. It is the largest landlocked country in the world.
question.clue: The Irtysh River passes through this country, which contains the cities of Aqtau and Atyrau and Lake Balkash.

swap.leadin: This empire's first ruler was Genghis Khan.
swap.text: Name this largest contiguous land empire in world history. It stretched from Siberia to Eastern Europe, eventually fracturing into several smaller realms such as the Chagatai Khanate.
swap.clue: This empire, which lost to the Mamluks at Ain Jalut, notoriously flung the bodies of plague-infested corpses with their counterweight trebuchets, spreading the Black Death.

question.leadin: The beginning of this war in 1979 led US president Jimmy Carter to boycott the 1980 Olympics in Moscow. --.
question.text: Identify this conflict between a communist power and a central Asian nation. The C.I.A. supplied the mujahedeen during this conflict.
question.clue: Operation Cyclone was an effort to fund one side in this conflict through the operation of the ISI, and was heavily promoted by men like Gust Avrakotos.

swap.leadin: This ruler defeated Tokhtamysh [TOKE-TAM-ISH] at the Battle of the Terek River. --.
swap.text: Name this conqueror from Samarkand who sacked Damascus and Delhi.
swap.clue: This man's victories at the Battles of the Kondurcha and Terek Rivers led to his defeat of Tokhtamysh and the Golden Horde.

question.text: This Khanate was known for conquering Kievan Rus and putting it under the "Mongol Yoke", which was eventually lifted by Ivan III. It was once led by Batu and is named for the color of the tents they used.
question.clue: Economically centered at Bolgary, its cities also included the capital Sarai.

swap.leadin: A political cartoon depicting this period shows Emir Sher Ali asking the reader to "save him from [his] friends"
swap.text: Name this Anglo-Russian conflict in the mid-1800s over Central Asia, which included the partitioning of Persia into spheres of influence, the Eastern Question, and the Anglo-Afghan wars.
swap.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

question.leadin: This city became a center of study in astronomy after the construction of an observatory by Ulugh Beg.
question.text: Name this city in the historical region of Transoxiana, which was revitalized under the reign of Timur.
question.clue: Herat replaced this city as capital under the reign of Shah Rukh.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about sacks of Delhi.
swap.text: This ruler sacked Delhi in 1398 by putting flaming bales of hay on the backs of camels, scattering the opposing war elephants. Often nicknamed for his limp, his conquests killed about 5% of the world's population.
swap.clue: The only time an Ottoman Sultan was captured in battle was duringthis man's victory at the Battle of Ankara against Bayezid Thunderbolt.

question.leadin: Answer the following relating to nuclear weapons treaties.
question.text: The United States refused to ratify the SALT II treaty after the Soviet Union invaded this country in 1979. The CIA provided arms to the Mujahedeen to help them repel the Soviets from this country.
question.clue: Reformed under Tarzi and Amanullah Khan, it saw turmoil during the Saur Revolution.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain country.
swap.text: Its first namesake war against the British occurred in 1838 when Dost Muhammad was deposed and then restored after a revolution in Kabul.
swap.clue: In 1977 Loya Jirga secured one party rule under the National Revolutionary Party under a President who was the cousin of former king Mohammad Zahir Shah.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of a mountainous nation that's been in the news a lot.
question.text: In 1893, the British set up this border between Afghanistan and Pakistan based on geographical features, not ethnic regions. This idiotic idea continues to lend itself today to ethnic tensions.
question.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

swap.leadin: This country's three largest tribes are called juz and were descended from the mythical figure Alash.
swap.text: Name this present-day country that briefly changed its capital's name to honor Nursaltan Nazarbayev, who led this country after it was the last to break away from the Soviet Union.
swap.clue: In 1989, a radioactive gas leak helped spur this country's independence movement.

question.text: Rulers of Rouran used this title that was later adopted by Bumin and the Gokturks. In the 13th century, this title was adopted by Temujin.
question.answerHtml: khan [or khagan; accept Genghis Khan or Chinggis Khan; prompt on emperor]
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.leadin: The BMAC is sometimes called the [this river] civilization, despite the fact that most of its sites were instead found around the Margiana.
swap.text: Name this river which separated the historical regions of Sogdiana and Bactria. A region named for being beyond this river was north of the ancient province of Khorasan.
swap.clue: A golden fish and a model chariot are among many items in an Achaemenid-era "treasure" named for this river.

question.text: The Afghan side at Panipat was led by this ruler, who had previously invaded India as a general of Nader Shah. This ruler united the Pashtun tribes to form the first modern Afghan state under the Durrani dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Ahmad Shah Durrani [accept Ahmad Shah Abdali; prompt on Shah Durrani or Shah Abdali alone]
question.clue: This cavalry commander discovered the leader of the Afsharid kingdom assassinated in a tent, prompting him to abscond with the royal seal and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

swap.leadin: Agdam, a city in this country, produced the best known Soviet fortified wine, or bormutchka, until its grape fields were razed to form defensive structures in the 1990s.
swap.text: Name this country that contests Nagorno-Karabakh with Armenia.
swap.clue: Soldiers from this country murdered thousands of people of a neighboring ethnicity in the 1920 Shusha Massacre over the status of Nagorno-Karabakh.

question.text: Under Mandukhai, the Northern Yuan defeated this western Mongol subgroup. A branch of this group moved further west to Russia and became the Kalmyks.
question.clue: The Khoshut were one of four tribes comprising this Mongol subgroup, who rivaled the Tumeds and later founded the Kalmyk Khanate. A leader of these people captured the Zhengtong ("JUNG-tong") emperor in one military campaign.

swap.leadin: The western movement of the Xiongnu confederacy pushed these people south, which in turn pushed the Sacae into the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom.
swap.text: Name these Tocharian-speaking nomads who, along with the Wusun, were visited by the Han diplomat Zhang Qian, who reported on their one hundred thousand horse archers.
swap.answerHtml: Yuezhi [accept Greater Yuezhi or Lesser Yuezhi; prompt on, but DO NOT REVEAL, Kushans]
swap.clue: This Central Asian people whose "Greater" branch migrated into the Ili Valley in the 160s BCE after the Xiongnu ("sh'yung-noo") defeated them. Kujula Kadphises ("koo-JOO-la kad-FYE-seez") later united these people and founded the Kushan Empire.

question.text: This "dog of war," along with Batu Khan, devastated Hungarian forces at the Battle of Mohi as the master strategist of the Mongol army under Genghis Khan and Ogedei Khan.
question.clue: He often commanded alongside Jebe, his fellow noyan, in battles such as Kalka River where he defeated the Cumans and Kievan Rus.

swap.text: This Khereid princess became Genghis Khan's daughter-in-law when she married his youngest son Tolui. She was the mother of the khans Mongke, Kublai, and Hulagu.
